items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Leonard Bernstein was the first student at Tanglewood, in 1940. He was a conducting student. So I took that program over.

ctx.x: Why is that, do you think?

I’ll answer it in a second. The other way that I’ve done it – you asked the question about how can I pass this on – I’ve been teaching conducting for 40 years now. I started – actually, I never thought I would teach conducting. I’m very modest about my accomplishments. I don’t think I need to be a teacher. But what happened – at Tanglewood, when I became artistic director there, I was first of all in charge of all the contemporary music, and then branched out again into the standard repertory, classical music. We…
over and conducting through their legs and whatever, they don’t get the job, because audiences want to see somebody.
